answer_text:
Here is a well-rounded **7-Day China Trip Itinerary** following the classic "Golden Triangle" route — **Beijing → Xi'an → Chengdu** — perfect for first-time visitors who want history, culture, nature, and incredible food!

---

# 🇨🇳 7-Day China Trip Itinerary: Beijing → Xi'an → Chengdu

For a well-balanced 7-day China itinerary, popular destinations like Beijing, Xi'an, and Chengdu offer iconic attractions and convenient transportation. These major cities have frequent high-speed trains and flights, giving you more flexibility and saving valuable travel time.

---

## 📍 Day 1 — Arrive in Beijing
- Fly into **Beijing Capital International Airport**. Take the Airport Express train to the city center for ¥25 — it's a better option than taxis during rush hour.
- Spend your first evening exploring the **Wangfujing Street** for a taste of local street food.
- Check into your hotel and rest up for a big day ahead.

---

## 📍 Day 2 — Beijing: Forbidden City & Tiananmen Square
- Visit the most iconic sights in and around the capital city, including the **Forbidden City** and the historic **Tiananmen Square**.
- Stroll through **Jingshan Park** for a panoramic view of the Forbidden City.
- In the evening, visit the vibrant **Wangfujing Night Market** for Peking duck and local delicacies.

---

## 📍 Day 3 — Beijing: The Great Wall & Summer Palace
- Head to the **Great Wall of China** — visit the **Mutianyu section**, which is less busy than Badaling and offers better views. Take the early bus to get more time at the wall.
- In the afternoon, visit the **Summer Palace**. It is an exceptional place and cannot be skipped from a Beijing itinerary. Located 15 kilometers away from central Beijing, the Summer Palace was used as a summer retreat by the Chinese royal family.
- At night, take the overnight train to Xi'an. Book a top bunk if you want more privacy at a lower price.

---

## 📍 Day 4 — Xi'an: Terracotta Army & Muslim Quarter
- Marvel at the world-renowned **Terracotta Army**, an extraordinary underground army guarding China's first emperor.
- In the evening, check out the food stalls in the **Muslim Quarter**. Try Yang Rou Pao Mo (bread in lamb soup), but ask them to go light on the oil if you're not used to rich food.
- Later, visit the historic **Giant Wild Goose Pagoda**. An optional evening trip to **Great Tang All Day Mall** offers lively performances and Tang-style architecture.

---

## 📍 Day 5 — Xi'an: City Wall & Travel to Chengdu
- Ride a bike along the ancient **Xi'an City Wall**, one of the best-preserved city walls in China. You can rent a bike for ¥45 to ride the 14km wall circuit.
- Take the afternoon **bullet train to Chengdu**. Get to the station 90 minutes early for passport checks.
- End your day with **Sichuan hotpot** — but be ready for serious heat!

---

## 📍 Day 6 — Chengdu: Giant Panda Base & Local Culture
- Get to the **Giant Panda Breeding Center** when it opens at 7:30 AM to see the pandas eat breakfast. No trip to China is complete without visiting the pandas — watch these adorable creatures munching bamboo in their natural habitat.
- Later, visit **People's Park** to watch locals play mahjong and practice tai chi. Finish your day in the **Kuanzhai Xiangzi (Wide & Narrow Alleys)**, where old meets new.
- Enjoy a relaxing **Sichuan tea ceremony** in one of the local teahouses.

---

## 📍 Day 7 — Chengdu: Leshan Giant Buddha (Day Trip) & Departure
- Leshan, which is a 1.5-hour bullet train ride from Chengdu, is home to the **world's largest carved stone Buddha**. You can visit this as a day trip on one of the tourist buses. The sheer size of the Buddha is overwhelming, as it stretches more than 71 meters into the sky.
- Return to Chengdu in the evening and fly home. Take metro line 1 directly to the airport for ¥4.

---

## ✈️ Travel Tips

- **Visas:** China currently offers visa-free entry for up to 30 days to ordinary passport holders from 47 countries, including much of Europe, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan, and several South American nations. A 7-day trip fits easily within this allowance. Always verify the latest requirements before booking.
- **Best Time to Visit:** China is a year-round destination for most of its popular regions. The main exceptions are high-altitude areas like Tibet and mountainous scenic spots such as Zhangjiajie and Huangshan, where heavy snow may close trails between December and February.
- **Getting Around:** High-speed trains are the best way to travel between cities — fast, affordable, and reliable.
- **Apps:** Download a translation app before you go, as English signage can be limited in some areas.

---

Enjoy your incredible journey through China! 🐉🏯🐼
